dct_description_sm: These images are called true-color or natural color because this combination of wavelengths is similar to what the human eye would see. The images are natural-looking images of land surface, oceanic and atmospheric features. The downside of this set of bands is that they tend to produce a hazy image.

This Corrected Reflectance (True Color) layer is from the Ocean Color Instrument (OCI), which is a spectrometer aboard NASA's Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) satellite. The sensor resolution is 1.2 km, imagery resolution is 1 km, and the temporal resolution is daily.

A daily visualization from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), available from 2024-02-25 and updated as new data arrive. Made from PACE OCI Level-2 Regional Surface Reflectance Data, version 3.1 (PACE_OCI_L2_SFREFL, version 3.1, doi:10.5067/PACE/OCI/L2/SFREFL/3.1).
